title: AI-assisted tests: GraphQL contracts and requirement traceability
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects ai-assisted tests: graphql contracts and requirement traceability with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The local GraphQL capstone creates candidate cases, validates them and exports pytest-compatible definitions.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Generated tests are candidates that require independent validation. For GraphQL, inspect operations, arguments, required fields, nullability, enum values and authorization rules. A syntactically valid query may fail business rules; an HTTP 200 response may contain GraphQL errors.

Requirement traceability connects each candidate to the rule it tests. Count unique covered behaviors, not the number of generated files. Positive, negative, boundary, authentication and authorization cases should remain distinct.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse the schema and operation AST rather than splitting schema text with fragile string rules. Build a coverage matrix for required arguments, invalid enums, nullable/non-null fields, malformed operations and permission rules. Generate structured case definitions with expected data/errors.

For REST, use OpenAPI contracts and domain examples. For locator suggestions, validate candidates against the DOM and require uniqueness and stability. Regression selection uses dependency edges and historical risk; it must not exclude mandatory critical tests.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A generated GraphQL test asserts only status 200 and passes when errors contains an authorization failure. A locator suggestion uses a dynamic index that happens to work once. Duplicate paraphrased cases inflate coverage statistics.

Compile/type-check candidates, execute against synthetic fixtures, inspect assertions and retain requirement IDs. Mutate a required field or expected value to prove the test can detect the intended failure.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The local GraphQL capstone creates candidate cases, validates them and exports pytest-compatible definitions. Its report shows requirement coverage, duplicates, execution failures and rejected unsupported operations.

An SDET owns acceptance: generated text becomes useful automation only after executable assertions demonstrate the target behavior. Never treat a model's self-reported completeness as test coverage evidence.

mistake: A generated GraphQL test asserts only status 200 and passes when errors contains an authorization failure. A locator suggestion uses a dynamic index that happens to work once. Duplicate paraphrased cases inflate coverage statistics.
takeaway: The local GraphQL capstone creates candidate cases, validates them and exports pytest-compatible definitions.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def graphql_ok(response):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def graphql_ok(response):
    return isinstance(response,dict) and not response.get('errors') and response.get('data') is not None
exercise.tests:
assert graphql_ok({'data':{'item':1}})
assert not graphql_ok({'data':None,'errors':[{'message':'bad'}]})
assert not graphql_ok({'data':{'item':1},'errors':[{'message':'partial'}]})
